note: Where each generation of the spine stands. THIS ARCHIVE'S JUDGEMENT, not the tree's. Read by /direct-line/ and by the homepage ladder, so the two can never disagree about whether a generation is proved.

@I20@: Birth, marriage, death and burial all recorded, and a three-part eulogy delivered by his own children survives in the family's hands.
@I76@: Born Brisbane 1892, died there suddenly on 10 November 1936 aged 44; the Courier-Mail carried both an obituary and a funeral notice. Sergeant 11335, 12th Australian Depot Unit of Supply — enlisted 13 December 1915, married nine weeks before he sailed, home in July 1919. A grocer who failed in 1926. His death at 44 is the hinge of the next generation's childhood.
@I208@: Born Brisbane 5 May 1864, the first generation born in the colony of Queensland; Chief Clerk of the Railway Department. Found dead in the kitchen of his house at Banyo on 21 March 1931 and buried at South Brisbane Cemetery, Dutton Park — the cemetery record confirms 1864, so the newspaper's 'aged 76' at the inquest is an error for 66.
@I381@: Born Parramatta 1829, christened at St James's Sydney that November — the register entry names his father George Pitt Darcy and his mother Maria. Schooled at The King's School, Parramatta; pastoral work and the California goldfields; then Queensland in 1863 and the Colonial Secretary's Office until his death.
@I647@: Major, 39th Regiment of Foot, thirty-four years in it. Commanded the regiment at Orthes, 27 February 1814, and was given a gold medal for it that took four years to reach him. Brought a detachment of thirty men out as the guard on the convict ship England, with his wife and baby daughter in the cabin, reaching Port Jackson 18 September 1826. Died at Parramatta 22 July 1849; six newspapers carried the notice. His birth year is the one soft spot: they say he was 69, which gives 1780, and the tree says 1783.
@I1059@: Documented from commission to grave. Connolly's Roll of Officers of the Corps of Royal Engineers, entry 203: second lieutenant 17 January 1776, lieutenant-colonel 29 April 1802, colonel 1813, major-general 12 August 1819, C.B.; Minorca, Portugal, Copenhagen, Walcheren; 'Died at Chatham, 13 5 1827'. Married Jean Ward at Portsea 21 June 1779; a son christened at Bridgetown, Barbados, in 1786; buried at St Mary, Chatham, 19 May 1827. Everything ABOVE him is a different matter entirely.
@I1872@: The inserted generation, and the weakest link in the chain. Said to have been born at St James's Palace, with two birth years sixty-nine years apart. The Earls of Holderness are a documented family; a son of theirs who founds a Portsmouth line is not, on present evidence, one of them. Nothing below this man depends on him — the line stands perfectly well without him.
